COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
C482 No.2362 of 2023
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel, along with
Mr. Naveen Singh Bisht, learned counsel for the
applicant.
2. Mr. Saurabh Pandey, learned Brief Holder for
the State.
3. Ms. Neeti Rana, learned counsel for the
respondent nos. 2 & 3.
4. Present compounding application (IA No.01
of 2023) has been filed, which is supported with the
affidavit of the real uncle Rajesh Singh, S/o
Raghuveer Singh, R/o Village Talli Kimoli, District
Chamoli, of the present applicant and also
supported with the affidavit of respondent no.2, the
mother of the victim, as well as the affidavit of the
respondent no.3, the victim. The uncle of the victim
Mr. Rajesh Singh who is present in the court as well
as respondent no. 2 and 3 are identified by the
respective counsels through their Aadhar Card.
5. The compounding affidavit is not supported
with the affidavit of the applicant- Manish Kandari,
since he is still in jail.
6. It is submitted by the counsel for the parties,
as pleaded in the affidavit filed in support of the
compounding application, that the applicant was
earlier granted short term bail, and the basis of grant
of short term bail was that the applicant had agreed
to marry the respondent no.3, the victim, and the
marriage card was also placed on record in the short
term bail application, and as per the marriage card,

the marriage was scheduled to be held on
30.10.2023. The short term bail application was
allowed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court by
order dated 22.09.2023, but the applicant could not
be released due to non-inclusion of Section 5/6 of
the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences
Act, 2012.
7. Since the applicant could not be released
even on short term bail, and he is still in jail, this is
the reason why this compounding application is not
supported with the affidavit of the applicant.
8. Today, the mother of the victim is present
before this Court along with her husband and this
Court interacts with the parents of the victim. They
submit that they both are agreed to marry their
daughter/victim with the applicant-Manish Kandari,
and they do not want to proceed with this case.
9. On interaction with the real uncle of the
applicant, he submits that he is the brother of the
father of the applicant, who is also agreeable to this
marriage along with the other family members.
10. Undoubtedly, at the time of the incident, the
victim was minor. However, now, today, she is
above 18 years of age, as her date of birth is
28.10.2005, and according to this, today, she is 18
years, 1 month, 9 days old. The statement of the
victim was also recorded as PW1 in the Court
below, wherein, she has stated that she was in love
with the applicant and since inception of their
relationship, she wants to marry the applicant. She
has stated that she does not want to proceed further
in these proceedings since she wants to marry the
applicant.
11. The learned counsel for the applicant placed
reliance on the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble
Bombay High Court in the case of Shakil Ahmed
Shaikh and Another Vs. State of Maharashtra and

Another, decided on 23.03.2023, wherein, in Para
No.7, the Hon'ble Bombay High Court observed
that, "if the victim attains the age of majority after
lodging of the report and they happily marry and
reside under one shelter and leading peaceful life as
a husband and wife, therefore, the continuity of the
proceedings would be nothing but a futile exercise."
The Hon'ble Bombay High Court also relied upon
the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case
of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and Another,
(2012) 10 SCC 303.
12. Here, in the present case, the marriage could
not be solemnized on the ground that the short term
bail was granted, but due to some inadvertent
mistake, the applicant could not be released, due to
non-adding of Section 5/6 of the Protection of
Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, in the
short term bail application, but now, today, though
the applicant is in jail, but the victim along with her
parents are present in the Court and this Court also
interacted with each of them, and they submit that
they all agreed for the marriage of the victim with
the applicant, and as and when the applicant is
released from jail, immediately, they will solemnize
their marriage.
13. Per Contra, learned State Counsel would
submit that though the offences are serious in nature
and cannot be compounded, but, he fairly submits
that earlier, the short term bail was granted on the
basis that they both agreed to marry each other, for
which the marriage invitation card was also
annexed, but the applicant could not be released,
due to non-adding of some Section. Now, learned
State Counsel submits that since the victim is
agreed, who, as on today is major, and her parents
are also agreed to their marriage, therefore, this
compounding application may be allowed.

14. The learned counsel for the parties further
submitted that the Coordinate Bench of this Court,
in identical set of circumstances, compounded the
offences which the State Counsel has not disputed.
15. After hearing the arguments, as advanced on
behalf of the parties, this Court is of the view that
the compounding application deserves to be
allowed.
16. Accordingly, the compounding application is
allowed.
17. For an interim measure, further proceedings
of Special Sessions Trial No. 14 of 2023. State
versus Manish Kandari, in the file of Special
Sessions Judge Chamoli, for the offences
punishable under Sections 376, 354-C, 506 IPC &
Section 5/6 of the Protection of Children from
Sexual offence (POCSO) Act, arising out of FIR
No.08 of 2023, P.S. Karnprayag, District Chamoli,
are quashed.
18. It is made clear that if the applicant refuses to
marry with the victim, the victim and her parents
are free to approach this Court again.
19. In view of this, present C-482 application is
also disposed of.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 07.12.2023 R.Bisht
